question: In Python, an if-statement allows code to be executed only if the condition is true.
An if-statement can only have a single condition to evaluate.
It is possible to execute multiple statements when the condition of an if-statement is true.
The 'else' part of an if-else statement is mandatory.
An if-statement must end with a colon in Python.
You can replace all if-statements with switch statements in Python.
In an if-elif-else chain, all the conditions are evaluated even after one condition is true.
An if-statement can be used to evaluate both the truth value of a condition and the execution of specific functions simultaneously.
Using nested if-statements in Python allows for more complex decision-making processes.
Python if-statements, by default, evaluate the condition and proceed with short-circuit evaluation.
